root_cause.text: In `sev_ioctl_do_pek_csr()` in the CCP/SEV ioctl path, the code copied the CSR blob back to userspace even when `__sev_do_cmd_locked()` reported a PSP/firmware failure, so an invalid-length error could make it use the firmware-reported length and read past the kernel-allocated buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_blob;` before `copy_to_user(input_address, blob, input.length);`, and the commit message says “don’t attempt to copy the blob to userspace if the firmware command failed” because “copying the number of bytes firmware requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace”; the KASAN report shows the overflow occurs in `sev_ioctl_do_pek_csr+0x31f/0x590` during `copy_to_user()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the comment describing how the PEK CSR length returned by firmware is propagated to userspace.
intent_record.what: The comment above `input.length = data.len;` was replaced. The old single-line comment stating that querying the CSR length means firmware responded with expected data was removed and replaced with a multi-line comment explaining that firmware returns the CSR blob length (either the minimum required length or the actual length written) and that this length is returned to the user.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter executable code or control flow; it only clarifies the meaning of the returned CSR length in the source. Runtime behavior remains the same, with `input.length` still being assigned `data.len` and copied back to userspace.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early error exit in PEK/CSR handling to avoid copying out data after a failed operation.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was inserted after the existing call that sets `ret`: `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_blob;`. This causes the function to jump to the `e_free_blob` cleanup path when `ret` is nonzero or when `argp->error` is set, before any `copy_to_user()` call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now stops early and frees the allocated blob if the PEK/CSR processing reported an error or if the command structure contains an unexpected error state. This prevents continuing with user-space copying after a failed operation and avoids using potentially invalid output data.

grouping_result.intent: Clarify the comment describing how the PEK CSR length returned by firmware is propagated to userspace.
Add an early error exit in PEK/CSR handling to avoid copying out data after a failed operation.

relevance_review.reason: The change is only a comment clarification about PEK CSR length handling and does not alter the ioctl logic that copied the CSR back on firmware failure or the unsafe length usage described in the vulnerability.
The change directly matches the root cause by adding an early error exit in PEK/CSR handling, preventing CSR data from being copied to userspace after a firmware/PSP command failure.

candidates.rationale: This is the point where the code proceeds to copy the CSR blob back to userspace. Because the pre-fix path did not exit early on __sev_do_cmd_locked() failure, execution could reach this copy-out using an invalid firmware-reported length and a kernel buffer that was not safe to expose.

This statement performs the usercopy that becomes unsafe when the earlier PSP/firmware command failed but the code still uses input.length from firmware. It is the direct operation that can read past the allocated kernel buffer and leak invalid data.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the point where the code enters the copy-out path for the CSR blob. In the vulnerable flow, execution could still reach this block even after __sev_do_cmd_locked() failed, allowing use of a firmware-reported length that was not safe.

This is the actual usercopy that becomes unsafe when the PSP/firmware command fails but the code continues anyway. Using input.length from firmware in that case can cause a read past the kernel-allocated buffer and leak invalid data.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown commit introduces the SEV_PEK_CSR ioctl path and the vulnerable pattern is present: it calls the firmware command and then copies the CSR blob back without checking for firmware failure before using the returned length. In this commit version, the root cause exists because the code would trust the PSP-reported size after `__sev_do_cmd_locked()` and use it in the userspace copy, which matches the described out-of-bounds read scenario. There is no fix visible here such as rejecting the copy on command failure or clamping the length against the kernel buffer size, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
